US-119-HR9785.title: South Dakota Water Feasibility Studies Act

actions.text: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 760.
Reported (Amended) by the Committee on Natural Resources. H. Rept. 119-863.
Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by Unanimous Consent.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9785.description: To direct the Secretary of the Interior to conduct studies to determine the feasibility of constructing projects to supply municipal, rural, and industrial water in certain parts of the Missouri River basin, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9785.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Interior Department to study whether three water supply projects could be built for towns, rural areas, and industry in parts of the Missouri River basin. The studies would cover the Western Dakota Regional Water System, an expansion of the Lewis and Clark Regional Water System, and the Dakota Mainstem Water Supply Project. For two of the studies, the federal share of study costs could not be more than $10 million or more than 50% of the total, and the authority would end 7 years after enactment.

US-119-HR10950.title: Data Center Oversight Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10950.description: To require sponsors of large data centers to file public disclosure statements with the Secretary of Energy, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10950.aiSummary: The bill would require sponsors of large data centers to file public disclosure statements with the Secretary of Energy. The reports would cover details like the site, power use, water use, labor, and costs that may affect electric bills, and they would be posted in a public online database. It would apply to new and some existing facilities and could bring civil penalties for failing to file correct reports.

US-119-HR10136.description: To require the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Crossett Experimental Forest to the State of Arkansas, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10136.aiSummary: The bill would require the Agriculture Secretary to transfer the Crossett Experimental Forest in Arkansas to the state if Arkansas asks for it within 180 days after enactment. The state would have to pay the transfer costs and keep the land as the Crossett Experimental State Forest for research, education, and demonstration work, with access for the University of Arkansas at Monticello and the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture. If the state does not meet the required use and care rules, the land could be returned to the United States.

US-119-HR10895.title: Teaching Engaged Citizenship Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on House Administration, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10895.description: To direct the Secretary of Education to establish a Civic Education and Service Learning Grant Program, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10895.aiSummary: The bill would have the Education Department create a grant program for civic education and service learning in public elementary and secondary schools. It would give grants to state and local school agencies, colleges, and nonprofit groups to train teachers, build civics lessons, and run student projects like mock hearings and community service, and it would authorize $400 million each fiscal year. It would also set up an Office of Civic Education, an advisory committee, and a center to study and improve these programs.

US-119-HR10873.title: AI Cyber Defense Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10873.description: To require the National Institute of Standards and Technology to carry out certain activities regarding certain artificial intelligence attacks, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10873.aiSummary: The bill would direct the National Institute of Standards and Technology, or NIST, to work with private AI companies on ways to define and stop certain AI distillation attacks. It would also create an AI Cybersecurity Roundtable to develop voluntary standards and best practices for using AI to help protect computer systems. NIST would publish these standards and best practices on its website after they are ready.

US-119-HR10851.title: Socket Full of Sunshine Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10851.description: To amend the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to establish a Federal standard for States to consider measures to promote portable solar generation devices, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10851.aiSummary: The bill would set a federal standard for states to consider ways to promote portable solar devices that plug into a home outlet and help cut electricity use. It would also create a grant program for states to give point-of-sale rebates of up to $1,000 for low- and moderate-income households, with extra focus on renters, multifamily residents, and high-energy burdened communities. The bill would require a voluntary label showing expected electricity cost savings and would direct a federal safety standard for these devices. It also sets some tenant protections, state review timelines, and authorizes $100 million a year for fiscal years 2027 through 2032.

US-119-S5690.title: Renewing the Dream Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources under authority of the order of the Senate of 09/30/2026.

US-119-S5690.description: A bill to provide for the replacement of the plaque at Lincoln Memorial commemorating the "I Have a Dream" speech of Martin Luther King, Jr.
US-119-S5690.aiSummary: The bill would require the Interior Secretary to replace the plaque at the Lincoln Memorial that marks Martin Luther King Jr.’s "I Have a Dream" speech. It would also use the federal law for memorials and plaques to guide the new plaque’s design and placement. The department could accept donations for the work, and federal funds could also be used.

US-119-HR10796.title: United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Armed Services, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10796.description: To direct the Secretary of Defense to designate an executive agent responsible for synchronizing cooperative efforts between the United States and Israel, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10796.aiSummary: The bill would require the Secretary of Defense to name one person or office to coordinate U.S. defense technology work with Israel. It would cover research, testing, buying, and joint work in areas like missile defense, cyber defense, artificial intelligence, and counter-drone systems. It would also require briefings and yearly reports to Congress on progress.

US-119-HR10774.title: SWIMS Act of 2026
US-119-HR10774.summary:
Strengthening Welfare in Marine Settings Act of 2026 or the SWIMS Act of 2026

This bill establishes prohibitions on capturing, importing, exporting, or breeding of orcas, beluga whales, false killer whales, or pilot whales for the purpose of public display.

Specifically, the bill prohibits the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration from issuing any permit under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 that authorizes the taking (e.g., capturing) or importation of such orcas or whales for the purpose of public display. The bill further revises the act to make it unlawful to export such orcas or whales, unless they are being transported to marine mammal sanctuaries or for release into the wild.

Further, the bill makes it unlawful under the Animal Welfare Act for any person to breed or artificially inseminate such marine mammals for purposes of using their progeny for public display.
US-119-HR10774.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2026-10-09)

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources, and in addition to the Committee on Agriculture, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10774.aiSummary: The bill would ban taking, importing, exporting, or breeding certain whales and orcas for public display. It would block federal permits for those actions and make it illegal to export them unless they are going to a marine mammal sanctuary or back to the wild. It would also bar breeding or artificial insemination of these animals when their young would be used for public display.

US-119-HR10752.title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10752.description: To establish in the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency of the Department of Homeland Security a task force on artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10752.aiSummary: The bill would set up an artificial intelligence task force inside the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency at the Department of Homeland Security. The task force would help guide the agency’s work on safe and secure AI, including cyber risks, workforce gaps, privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties. It would also give briefings to House and Senate homeland security committees every 6 months, and the task force would end 5 years after the law takes effect.

US-119-HR10730.title: Healthy Communities Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10730.description: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify the premium tax credit, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10730.aiSummary: The bill would change the health insurance premium tax credit, which helps people pay for coverage, and it would start for tax and plan years after December 31, 2025. It would also add help for some people in the Medicaid coverage gap, change some Medicaid funding rules for states, and set open enrollment dates for coverage starting in 2026. In addition, it would add fraud checks and penalties for agents and brokers who help enroll people in exchange plans.

US-119-HR10675.title: BUILD with Allies Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10675.description: To strengthen critical mineral, energy, manufacturing and technology supply chains, advance innovation and allied cooperation, enhance United States technological leadership and competitiveness, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10675.aiSummary: The bill would set up programs to work with allied countries on critical minerals, energy, manufacturing, and technology supply chains. It would also create exchange and cooperation programs, a list of foreign mining entities tied to forced labor or environmental harm, and steps to help foreign partners buy U.S.-made cyber and digital technology. Other parts would address trade, development aid, and shipbuilding competition with China.

US-119-HR10532.title: Beagle Liberation Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10532.description: To require the humane transfer of certain retired research dogs and cats, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10532.aiSummary: The bill would require some research facilities that receive federal funding to make reasonable efforts to transfer retired dogs and cats to an adoption group. A veterinarian would have to certify certain cases before the animal could be euthanized. It would apply to live domestic dogs and cats used for research, testing, breeding, or education.

US-119-HR10455.title: Debt-Free College Act of 2026
US-119-HR10455.summary:
Debt-Free College Act of 2026

This bill establishes measures to cover the unmet financial need of students who are enrolled at certain institutions of higher education (IHEs). Unmet financial need refers to the difference between a student's cost of attendance and the student's student aid index, plus any federal, state, and local sources of grant aid. In addition, the bill makes certain Dreamer students (i.e., students who have been granted Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals status and who entered the United States before the age of 16) eligible for federal financial aid.

First, the bill requires the Department of Education (ED) to award grants for state-federal partnerships with a goal of providing debt-free college for all eligible students at in-state public IHEs. Eligible student refers to an individual who (1) is enrolled or is eligible to enroll in an in-state public IHE, and (2) completes a Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) or demonstrates eligibility for a Federal Pell Grant through state or institutional financial aid eligibility forms.

Next, the bill requires ED to award grants to historically Black colleges and universities and minority-serving institutions to cover the unmet financial need of enrolled students.

ED must establish an office to administer grants and provide oversight.

In addition, the bill makes Dreamer students who entered the United States before the age of 16 who meet certain educational criteria eligible for federal student aid.
US-119-HR10455.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2026-09-16)

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10455.aiSummary: The bill would create grants to help cover the gap between college costs and other aid for students at certain colleges. It would support state and federal partnerships to help eligible students at in-state public colleges attend debt free, and it would give grants to historically Black colleges and universities and other minority-serving schools for this purpose. It would also make some Dreamer students, who were brought to the U.S. before age 16 and meet certain school rules, eligible for federal student aid.

US-119-HR10334.title: EFIN Verification Act of 2026
US-119-HR10334.summary:
EFIN Verification Act of 2026

This bill requires the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or a specified validator (e.g., software provider or state agency) to validate that an electronic filing identification number (EFIN) is authorized and active before a federal tax return or other document may be electronically filed with the IRS. (As background, an EFIN is assigned by the IRS to an individual or entity who is authorized to file federal tax returns and other documents on behalf of other taxpayers.)

Specifically, the bill requires (1) the IRS to develop a program to validate the status of an EFIN in real time, and (2) EFINs to be validated prior to the initial use and at intervals determined by the IRS.
US-119-HR10334.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2026-09-10)

Introduced in House

US-119-HR10334.aiSummary: The bill would require the IRS, or another approved checker, to confirm that an electronic filing ID is active and allowed before a federal tax return or other document can be filed online. It would also require the IRS to build a system to check these IDs in real time and to verify them before first use and at set intervals. An electronic filing ID is a number the IRS gives to people or businesses that are allowed to file tax forms for others.

US-119-HR10257.title: To require the United States Postal Service to designate ZIP Codes for certain communities.

US-119-HR9521.title: Broadband Infrastructure Extension Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9521.description: To amend title VI of the Social Security Act to extend that date on which certain funds related to broadband infrastructure projects may be expended.
US-119-HR9521.aiSummary: The bill would give more time to use certain federal funds for broadband infrastructure projects. It would let state and local fiscal recovery funds be spent through September 30, 2027, for those projects. It would also let Capital Projects Fund money for broadband projects be spent before January 1, 2028.

US-119-HR9367.title: Stop Lawmakers From Predicting Act

actions.text: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 5 - 4.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9367.description: To amend chapter 131 of title 5, United States Code, to restrict Members of Congress and their spouses and dependents from profiting off prediction markets, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9367.aiSummary: This bill would bar members of Congress, their spouses, and their dependent children from making or offering deals tied to prediction markets, such as bets based on government action or political outcomes. It would also let ethics offices give guidance and assess a fee if the rule is broken, with the money paid to the Treasury. The changes would take effect 180 days after the bill becomes law.

US-119-HR9224.title: Child Care Modernization Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on Financial Services, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9224.description: To amend the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to reauthorize and update the Act, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9224.aiSummary: The bill would update and reauthorize the federal child care grant law for fiscal years 2027 through 2031. It would change definitions and planning rules, including who can qualify for help, and would require states to consult parents, child care providers, employers, local governments, and tribal groups when making plans. It would also expand language on child care quality, training, safety checks, and mixed delivery systems, which use a mix of child care settings and programs.

US-119-HR9048.title: Celiac Safety Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9048.description: To amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to include gluten-containing grain in the definition of a major food allergen.
US-119-HR9048.aiSummary: The bill would add gluten-containing grains, such as wheat, rye, and barley, to the federal list of major food allergens. That would affect food makers and labels under the food safety law. The change would apply to food introduced into interstate commerce 18 months after the bill becomes law.
